research.summary: Neural networks for multipartite entanglement detection on a three-qubit NMR processor.
points: Designed an ANN that detects genuine multipartite entanglement and assigns one of six SLOCC classes to three-qubit states: 128 real features (Re and Im of the 64 elements of ρ), reduced to 18 (14 Re, 4 Im) by the canonical form, then ranked by ANOVA within the 18.

projects.name: Hybrid VQC Weather Forecasting with FPGA Inference
projects.blurb: 7-qubit variational circuit for 24-day temperature forecasting, with a custom kernel on an AMD Alveo FPGA for low-latency edge inference.
projects.abstract: A hybrid quantum-classical model that forecasts temperature 24 days ahead from daily NCMRWF reanalysis data, using a 7-qubit variational quantum circuit (50 parameters) with StronglyEntanglingLayers. For low-latency inference, the frozen model runs on a custom AMD Alveo U55C FPGA kernel built with HLS.
projects.role: Co-author (with first author N. Khan), IEEE TQCEBT 2026.

sections.p: 24-day-ahead temperature forecasting is hard: atmospheric dynamics are nonlinear and labelled data is limited. The question was whether a compact variational quantum circuit, trained on daily NCMRWF reanalysis data, could learn useful long-range patterns, and whether its inference could run fast enough for edge use.

The model is a 7-qubit variational quantum circuit with 50 trainable parameters, using angle encoding to map meteorological variables onto the qubits and two StronglyEntanglingLayers as the ansatz. It was trained, validated and tested in PennyLane on a CPU-based quantum simulator, reaching a test RMSE of 3.01 K and R² of 0.801.

For low-latency edge inference, the frozen model runs on a custom Vitis HLS kernel on an AMD Alveo U55C FPGA; the kernel exchanges batches of input features, pre-trained weights and expectation values with the host over HBM.
A hybrid VQC forecaster with low-latency FPGA inference for edge use. Published at IEEE TQCEBT 2026.

projects.name: Quantum Image Representation Neural Networks
projects.blurb: Quantum neural networks for binary image classification built on four quantum image encodings: NASS, QBIR, FTQR and FRQCI.
projects.abstract: Quantum neural networks that classify binary MNIST images (0 vs 1) at 2×2 to 16×16, plus a three-class FashionMNIST generalization study, with pixel data encoded through four quantum image representations: NASS, QBIR, FTQR and FRQCI. It compares circuit depth, gate count and qubit usage for the four encodings; QBIR gives the shallowest circuits, FRQCI the deepest. Published in The Journal of Supercomputing 82:495 (2026).

sections.p: Quantum image classification depends heavily on how classical pixel data is encoded into quantum states, but encodings are often chosen by convention rather than by measured trade-off.

I built quantum neural networks on four quantum image representations — NASS, QBIR, FTQR and FRQCI — for binary MNIST classification (0 vs 1) at 2×2 to 16×16, plus a three-class FashionMNIST generalization study. It compares circuit depth, gate count and qubit usage for the four encodings; QBIR gives the shallowest circuits, FRQCI the deepest. The paper also analyses trainability (gradient variance and norms) and expressivity, not just resource cost.
Published in The Journal of Supercomputing 82:495 (2026).

projects.paper: Quantum image representation-based quantum neural networks for binary classification

projects.name: Linear-Optical QKD Network Testbeds
projects.blurb: DPS, COW, and Twin-Field QKD simulated over realistic photonic channels with attack modelling.
projects.abstract: Simulation testbeds for differential-phase-shift (DPS), coherent-one-way (COW), and twin-field QKD protocols on linear-optical setups in OptiSystem and ANSYS, including loss, noise, and photonic channel impairments. Intercept-resend and photon-number-splitting attacks are modelled, and resource-state and entanglement generation benchmarked.
projects.role: DRDO Junior Research Fellow — protocol simulation and attack modelling.

sections.p: QKD protocols are usually analysed under idealised channel assumptions. Deployment behaviour depends on loss, detector noise, and attacker models that idealised analysis omits.

I built simulation testbeds for three protocols — differential-phase-shift (DPS), coherent-one-way (COW), and Twin-Field QKD — in OptiSystem and ANSYS, including loss, noise, and photonic channel impairments.
I modelled intercept-resend and photon-number-splitting attacks and benchmarked resource-state and entanglement generation.

projects.name: Quantum Circuits for Block Ciphers
projects.blurb: Mini-AES / S-AES circuits with a Grover-based plaintext–ciphertext attack demonstration.
projects.abstract: Quantum circuit designs for an 8-bit AES (Mini-AES / S-AES) with Galois-field arithmetic, run on Qiskit and IBM Quantum hardware, demonstrating Grover key search on a scaled-down cipher, which needs O(√N) oracle queries versus O(N) classically.
projects.role: Research intern — circuit design and attack demonstration.

sections.p: Understanding how symmetric ciphers degrade under quantum attack requires explicit, runnable circuit constructions, not just asymptotic arguments.
I built quantum circuits for an 8-bit AES (Mini-AES / S-AES), including the Galois-field arithmetic the S-box depends on, and ran them on Qiskit and IBM Quantum hardware.

I implemented a plaintext–ciphertext attack with Grover search and amplitude amplification, demonstrating Grover key search on a scaled-down cipher, which needs O(√N) oracle queries versus O(N) classically.

projects.name: Entanglement Detection via Neural Networks (NMR)
projects.blurb: An ANN that detects genuine multipartite entanglement and assigns SLOCC classes on a three-qubit NMR processor from 18 of 128 density-matrix elements.
projects.abstract: An artificial neural network that detects genuine multipartite entanglement and assigns one of six SLOCC classes to three-qubit states. Each density matrix gives 128 real features (Re and Im of the 64 elements of ρ); the canonical form reduces them to 18 (14 Re, 4 Im), which are then ranked by ANOVA. Validated on 30 experimental pseudopure states from an NMR quantum processor. Published in Quantum Information Processing 24(3), 74 (2025).
projects.role: Co-first author (equal contribution with V. Gulati); MS research student.

sections.p: Detecting genuine multipartite entanglement in experimental NMR systems is hard: witnesses are state-specific and full state tomography is experimentally costly. The trained model needs only a few elements (4 for GME, 6 for SLOCC), which points to reduced-measurement protocols; here they were read off reconstructed states.

I designed an ANN that detects genuine multipartite entanglement and assigns one of six SLOCC classes. Each state gives 128 real features (Re and Im of the 64 elements of ρ); writing states in canonical form leaves 18 (14 Re, 4 Im), which are then ranked by ANOVA within the 18.

Validated on 30 experimental three-qubit pseudopure states from an NMR processor: GME detection reached 0.954 ± 0.046 accuracy with 4 features, and SLOCC classification 0.867 ± 0.090 with 6 (overall accuracy over the experimental states, Tables IV–V).
Published in Quantum Information Processing 24(3), 74 (2025); preprint arXiv:2409.19739.

projects.name: VQLS for Financial Time-Series Forecasting
projects.blurb: A variational quantum linear solver applied end to end to next-day stock price forecasting on real market data.
projects.abstract: A variational quantum linear solver (VQLS) applied to time series forecasting on real financial market data. Hankel-like trajectory matrices are built from historical Reliance Industries stock prices and the resulting linear system is solved with a quantum-classical hybrid approach: Hadamard test circuits evaluate the cost function, COBYLA optimizes the variational parameters, and a SWAP test estimates the overlap of the solution state with recent market data to give the next-day forecast. Quantum advantage is not realized at this problem scale (2 × 2 system), and classical baselines reach equivalent accuracy; the workflow runs end to end on the Aer simulator with shallow circuits (depth ~6) compatible with NISQ hardware, and the paper identifies its scalability bottlenecks.

sections.p: Existing VQLS demonstrations focus on synthetic test cases; practical deployment on domain-specific data remains sparse. The question was whether the quantum-classical hybrid architecture can be validated on an authentic forecasting workflow before hardware scales.

A Hankel-like trajectory matrix is built from daily closing prices of Reliance Industries (January to April 2023) and decomposed into a Pauli basis. Hadamard test circuits evaluate the VQLS cost function, COBYLA optimizes the variational parameter with 10,000 shots per circuit, and a SWAP test estimates the overlap of the solution state with recent market data to give the next-day forecast. All circuits run in Qiskit on the Aer simulator.

The workflow runs end to end on the Aer simulator with shallow circuits (depth ~6) compatible with NISQ hardware, and the solution is verified against AR(1) and linear regression baselines. Quantum advantage is not realized at this 2 × 2 scale, and the classical baselines reach equivalent accuracy in negligible time. The paper identifies the scalability bottlenecks: exponential growth of the Pauli decomposition and COBYLA shot overhead.
Published by IEEE, 2026.

projects.paper: Variational Quantum Linear Solver for Time Series Forecasting: A Practical Implementation on Financial Data

projects.name: TensNet: Tensor Networks for 2D Flow Simulation
projects.blurb: A tensor network library using MPS and MPO for memory-efficient simulation of 2D incompressible flow.
projects.abstract: TensNet is a library implementing tensor network methods, using Matrix Product States (MPS) and Matrix Product Operators (MPO), for memory-efficient simulation of the 2D incompressible Navier–Stokes equations. It keeps solution accuracy through adaptive bond-dimension truncation, uses the DMRG algorithm to solve the implicit pressure-correction equations, and uses cross-approximation to handle complex immersed boundaries, reducing the memory footprint relative to traditional methods.

sections.p: Computational fluid dynamics simulations demand enormous memory for storing high-resolution velocity fields, which is a barrier to practical simulations on resource-constrained systems.

TensNet represents flow fields as Matrix Product States and operators as Matrix Product Operators, compressing them by SVD truncation with adaptive bond dimensions. The two-site DMRG algorithm solves the implicit Poisson equations in the pressure-correction scheme, and cross-approximation represents immersed boundaries and obstacle geometries as MPS.
Benchmarks include a cylinder in cross-flow and arrays of circular obstacles, with drag coefficients and Strouhal numbers compared against reference values.
Manuscript in preparation.

statement: My work connects quantum information research with production engineering: what it takes to run a quantum algorithm on hardware under real constraints (noise, latency, memory bandwidth) and keep it working reliably.

That has led me across three connected areas. In variational quantum algorithms and quantum machine learning, I study how data encoding and circuit structure affect resource cost (circuit depth, gate count, qubits) and how hybrid pipelines perform on real forecasting tasks. In quantum hardware acceleration, I compile trained variational circuits into state-vector simulation kernels on FPGA fabric for low-latency inference. In photonic quantum networks, I simulate QKD protocols over lossy channels and model intercept-resend and photon-number-splitting attacks.

My MS research at IISER Mohali used neural networks to detect genuine multipartite entanglement and classify SLOCC classes on a three-qubit NMR processor (co-first author, Quantum Information Processing, 2025).
I think quantum research moves faster when its artefacts are built like software: tested, versioned, reproducible and deployable.
